correctness.rationale: The ring Fourier product is a Chebyshev polynomial; cyclic equality of diagonal cofactors gives \(\det(zI-K)=P+i\gamma P\prime/N\) for every complex spectral variable. At each protected interior wavenumber the Chebyshev differential equation gives a nonzero characteristic derivative. The characteristic equation is even in flux detuning, and an analytic simple root has the exact negative imaginary quadratic coefficient with no quadratic real shift and a \(O(\delta^4)\) remainder. Strictly negative imaginary parts at generic flux follow from dissipativity and the nondegenerate plane-wave spectrum. Direct matrix checks of 33 determinants over ring sizes from 3 to 13 and 195 eigenvalue branches from 3 to 12 passed; finite checks are not the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: Zero-flux avoiding-mode existence and zero-flux trap arrangement classification are prior work (Krapivsky–Luck–Mallick); the new claim instead gives every protected mode’s exact second flux derivative and shows its real quadratic component is zero. A fluxed non-Hermitian continuum ring, a lossy three-site scattering AB element, and a single-scatterer open tight-binding chain do not assert that discrete ring curvature. Relevant direct and alternative-terminology searches found no dominating all-size eigenvalue-width result. Residual risk of obscure equivalent transfer-matrix results remains, so priority is self-reviewed, not independently certified.
residual_risks: Potential less-discoverable studies of the same flux-dependent rank-one secular equation could contain an equivalent curvature calculation.
The exact zero-flux avoiding-mode subspace is known and is not claimed as original.
The asymptotic does not control the global slowest mode or any joint limit in ring size and loss.
Independent priority and scientific audit have not been carried out.

value.rationale: A controlled flux error destroys the interference-protected subspace of a lossy ring. The proved mode-resolved lifetime coefficient is a natural quantitatively needed response, varies sharply with mode and ring size and reveals inverse-loss Zeno protection. Exact cancellation of the quadratic real shift separates dissipation from energy detuning and is not given by generic existence of dark modes. The result is all finite sizes and positive loss strengths, not an arbitrary finite calculation.
